lessons.title: Filter Rows
lessons.description: Implement filter_rows(rows, key, value) keeping dict rows where row[key]==value. The test checks that filter_rows(rows, 'a', 1) equals [{'a': 1}, {'a': 1}].
learning_objectives: Harbor clerks recount crates before dawn, and filter tabular dict rows.
lessons.solution_code:
def filter_rows(rows, key, value):
    return [r for r in rows if r.get(key) == value]

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — Dicts — dict.get(key) and list comprehensions

lessons.title: Select Columns
lessons.description: Implement select(rows, cols) returning new dicts with only cols. The test checks that select(rows, ['x', 'z']) equals [{'x': 1, 'z': 3}].
learning_objectives: Mesa clerks recount crates before dawn, and project columns from rows.
lessons.solution_code:
def select(rows, cols):
    return [{c: r[c] for c in cols if c in r} for r in rows]

lessons.title: Practice Inner Join
lessons.description: Implement inner_join(left, right, key) joining lists of dicts on key. The test checks that len(res) equals 1; inner_join(left, right, 'id')[0]['n'] equals 'a'; inner_join(left, right, 'id')[0]['s'] equals 10.
learning_objectives: Quarry clerks recount crates before dawn, and inner-join dict tables.

tests.name: test_inner_join
tests.unittest_code:
def test_inner_join(self):
    left = [{'id': 1, 'n': 'a'}, {'id': 2, 'n': 'b'}]
    right = [{'id': 1, 's': 10}, {'id': 3, 's': 30}]
    res = inner_join(left, right, 'id')
    self.assertEqual(len(res), 1)
    self.assertEqual(res[0]['n'], 'a')
    self.assertEqual(res[0]['s'], 10)

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — Mapping Types — dict.setdefault for grouping before joining
